prompt: Let A={u,v}, B={p,q,r}, C={0,1}. Let g:A→B and f:B→C be functions, and suppose f∘g:A→C is surjective. Determine which of the following properties are logically forced: (i) f is surjective; (ii) g is surjective; (iii) f is injective. Prove every forced property and give a fully specified countermodel for each property that is not forced.

Let X={0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7} and define T:X→X by T(0)=1, T(1)=2, T(2)=2, T(3)=4, T(4)=5, T(5)=3, T(6)=7, T(7)=7. Compute Im(T), every fibre T⁻¹({y}), the multiplicity μ(y)=|T⁻¹({y})| for each y∈X, all cycles, all fixed points, and for each x the number of steps before its orbit first enters its eventual cycle. Show a partition check for the fibres and a partition check for the basins of the cycles.

Using RFC 3986 §2.1 and §6.2.2.2, assess the following URI components: %7Ealice, ~alice, %2F, and /. Explain (a) whether hexadecimal letter case in percent-encoding matters, (b) when a percent-encoded octet may be decoded during normalization, and (c) whether %2F may generally be normalized to / without changing the reserved-character semantics. Cite the relevant RFC sections and distinguish a standards rule from an implementation-specific assumption.

A deterministic machine has hidden states S={s0,s1,s2,s3} and observed labels π(s0)=π(s1)=R, π(s2)=π(s3)=S. Its transition function is T(s0)=s2, T(s1)=s1, T(s2)=s2, T(s3)=s3. A report observes only the label sequence R,S,S,S,... starting from s0. Explain whether that single report establishes that the observed process has a unique deterministic successor from each observed label, and state a precise condition on T and π that would guarantee such a deterministic observed quotient. Give a counterexample using the supplied machine if the guarantee fails.

A researcher tests a function h:X→Y on a finite subset S⊊X and observes that h restricted to S is injective. They conclude that h is injective on all of X. Is the conclusion valid? Give the smallest possible finite counterexample with explicit X, Y, S, and h, and state an additional condition on the untested part of X that would make the inference valid.
